function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

messages.reasoning_content:
Now I understand. I need to implement `render_message(recipient, template_name)` in app/render.py:

1. Read the named UTF-8 file from templates dir
2. Render the complete Jinja2 template with `recipient` in context
3. Return full text unchanged, including final newline

Key considerations:
- Jinja2's `render` returns text. Templates end with a final newline. Jinja2 by default has `keep_trailing_newline=False`, which strips a single trailing newline from the template. The test expects `notice.j2` to render to `'To: Alice\nYour total is 42.\nSent with NotifyHub\n'` — with trailing newline. So I need `keep_trailing_newline=True`.
- Templates include expressions (`{{ 6 * 7 }}`), loops (`{% for %}` with `range`), and filters (`|upper`). `range` needs to be available — in Jinja2, `range` is available in templates by default (it's in the default namespace). Yes, Jinja2 provides `range` in the template globals by default.
- "Directory traversal is outside this interface" — so I don't need to guard against `../` paths; just read the file. But using FileSystemLoader with the template dir is fine. Actually, using `jinja2.FileSystemLoader(TEMPLATE_DIR)` and `env.get_template(template_name)` would be natural. FileSystemLoader actually guards against traversal (it splits and joins; pieces containing ".." would... actually FileSystemLoader joins path and checks). But the README says directory traversal is out of scope. Either approach works.

Should I use sandbox? The README says maintainer-authored templates only, no user input, so regular Environment is fine. The task says "maintainer-controlled complete Jinja2 template rendering" — templates are trusted. Use standard `jinja2.Environment`.

Implementation:

```python
"""Render versioned maintainer templates for the local notification/report tool."""
from pathlib import Path

from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader

TEMPLATE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'templates'

_env = Environment(
    loader=FileSystemLoader(TEMPLATE_DIR),
    keep_trailing_newline=True,
    autoescape=False,
)


def render_message(recipient: str, template_name: str) -> str:
    """Return the complete rendered local template; see README.md."""
    template = _env.get_template(template_name)
    return template.render(recipient=recipient)
```
